proposals.before: Four commands rank with the three dukes: Grand General first, then Palace Charging Cavalry, then Chariots and Cavalry, then Palace Guards.
proposals.after: Four commands rank with the three dukes: Grand General first, then Charging Cavalry, then Chariots and Cavalry, then Guards.
proposals.reason: 骠骑 and 卫 do not mean 'Palace'; the idiomatic gloss invents 'Palace' before Charging Cavalry and Guards.

proposals.before: At Guangwu's restoration Wu Han held Grand General merged with Grand Marshal; Jing Dan was Palace Charging Cavalry Grand General, still below ducal rank; many Front, Rear, Left, Right, and miscellaneous generals led field armies only to be disbanded when the fighting ended.
proposals.after: At Guangwu's restoration Wu Han held Grand General merged with Grand Marshal; Jing Dan was Charging Cavalry Grand General, still below ducal rank; many Front, Rear, Left, Right, and miscellaneous generals led field armies only to be disbanded when the fighting ended.
proposals.reason: Same invented 'Palace' before 骠骑; Chinese is 骠骑大将军.

proposals.before: Emperor Ming, seeing talent in his brother Prince Cang of Dongping, first named him Palace Charging Cavalry General;
proposals.after: Emperor Ming, seeing talent in his brother Prince Cang of Dongping, first named him Charging Cavalry General;
proposals.reason: Same invented 'Palace' before 骠骑将军.

proposals.before: As An's government weakened, Geng Bao—the empress's uncle by blood—held Grand General as a resident capital post.
proposals.after: As An's government weakened, Geng Bao—his full maternal uncle—held Grand General as a resident capital post.
proposals.reason: 嫡舅 is the emperor's maternal uncle (mother's full brother), not the empress's uncle.

decisions.reason: Chinese lists 骠骑将军 and 卫将军; neither title contains a palace/palace-guard sense, so the idiomatic 'Palace' before Charging Cavalry and Guards is invented.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 次骠骑将军，次车骑将军，次卫将军

decisions.reason: Chinese has 骠骑大将军 with no palace element; removing the invented 'Palace' restores the title accurately.
Chinese 以为骠骑将军 has no palace sense; the proposed title matches the source and the unit's literal rendering.
In context of 安帝, 嫡舅耿宝 is Emperor An's full maternal uncle, parallel to 舅邓骘 in s0088; the original wrongly makes him the empress's uncle.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 始以嫡舅耿宝为大将军
